<reason>Side A won the priority clash in the motion as written. B defended short-form mainly as a doorway to long-form depth and its durable value as in-house staff capability, which A turned into concessions against prioritizing creators and feeds over channels. A also gave cleaner answers on universality as guaranteed access rather than identical habits, staff journalists versus externally loyal creators, and regulated broadcast carriage versus revocable platform distribution.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>A's Rebuttal 2 was decisive: it distinguished internal staff brands from creators with pre-built followings and sponsors, then used B's BBC desk and capability argument to argue for funding staff and destination services rather than prioritizing creator partnerships.</best_rebuttal>
